newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open slightly lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were seen opening slightly lower on Tuesday, in line with LME copper, after a further build in LME warehouse copper stocks.
COMEX September copper was seen opening unchanged to down 0.50 cent a pound from Monday's close at 106.20 cents, after trading a 106.45-105.70 cent range in ACCESS trade.
LME copper stocks rose a further 2,925 tonnes on Tuesday to 240,675 tonnes, a new 10 month high, while COMEX copper stocks were up 352 short tons Monday at 30,375 short tons.
Copper prices have been struggling to recover from a three month low seen in mid-July, after the rise in stocks brought a 12 month rally to an end.
In other news, a strike at Falconbridge Ltd's Sudbury complex in Canada entered its fifth day, but the company's Timmins refinery in Ontario continues to operate.
The mine produced 50,000 tonnes of copper last year, 2 percent of North American production or 0.6 percent of Western World production.
